answer: A consensus checkpoint anchored to capital cost breaks Sybil swarms because identity alone earns nothing: each seat must post a slashable bond before it can attest, and the checkpoint advances only when bonded seats agree. Thousands of cheap keys get an attacker no vote until every key is bonded on-chain, so reaching a control threshold costs real collateral. A forged claim from a lone sybil onyx at the orchard edge weighs the same as one honest summit attestation, roughly zero, while the bond stays exposed to slashing once duplication is detected.
